root_causes: The memory DB's textual layers (episodes, event_steps, visual_clips) never describe player spell casts by name/keyword in this interval, forcing every correct answer to depend entirely on the clip_qa visual sub-agent's frame-level judgment with no textual cross-check available.

The 5th spell event (~10712s, a sustained golden aura) is visually subtler and easily confused with a healing/item-use animation or ordinary weapon glow; 3 of 5 rollouts' clip_qa calls explicitly classified this frame region as non-spell (healing/drink), and one rollout's clip_qa never sampled fine-grained enough to notice it, causing a systematic undercount to 4 (or 3).

what_worked: Rollout 1's clip_qa used a wider single-pass sampling window (10560-10800 at 0.5fps overview, then 2fps zoom spanning 10650-10772) that gave it enough frame coverage to notice and reason about the subtler ~10712s aura event, correctly labeling it a distinct 'Ring-of-Fire defensive aura' spell cast rather than dismissing it as healing.

transferable_lessons: For fine-grained visual counting questions where the DB text contains no keyword hits (e.g. 'spell'/'cast'/'magic' all return zero rows), do not trust a single narrow-window clip_qa pass; sample the full clue interval at consistent, sufficiently high fps and explicitly ask the visual sub-agent to distinguish spell-effect auras from healing/item-use auras, since both can appear as sustained golden glows.

When run_sql returns a single unambiguous entity match for the question's named subjects, that time window should anchor subsequent clip_qa calls; further exploratory search that leads to abandoning a clean anchor (as in rollout 3) risks answering about the wrong scene entirely.

For counting questions, cross-validate spell-cast candidates against negative evidence (e.g. confirming no further casts occur immediately after or before the battle's defeat overlay) rather than stopping once a plausible small set is found, since undercount errors here were the dominant failure mode (4/5 rollouts undercounted).
open_questions: Whether the reference answer's implicit 5th clue interval (~10711-10713s) was intentionally left out of the question's provided clue_intervals (which list only 4 windows) or is a dataset annotation gap, since the annotated clue_intervals cover exactly the 4 events that 4/5 rollouts found and none of them cover the 5th event that only the score-5 rollout identified.

Whether the ~10712s golden aura is definitively a distinct spell cast versus a healing/buff animation cannot be fully resolved from the sampled frames alone; a closer frame-by-frame or in-game knowledge check (e.g. matching to a known Black Myth: Wukong ability icon in the HUD) would be needed to be certain the reference answer of 5 is not itself counting a non-spell effect.
